items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: So he wrote up music. And I went around a couple of days later, and he passed me a sheet of music. Here was all the manuscript. All nicely done with the tune in there. And he says, you write words to this now.

ctx.x: Just the man. So we were going to do that. Then one day, he went down there. I don't know how much he tried to do on that. But he says, you know, Mr. Kerou, he says, the thing that is better now is songs. He says, I've got a couple of songs in my head. And he says, if we publish them, why, he says, I think they do better to start with than the Joplin stuff. So I said, well, you know more about it than I do. I said, go ahead and write them up and make them complete. So he wrote up music. And I went around a couple…
On the New Orleans series over TV.

items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: He said, here. He wrote it unhanded to me. He says, you write words to it. Well, I cracked my skull. And I finally got words to the chorus.

ctx.x: Did you ever know a person who played with him here in Washington named John W. Dews? No. I encountered this man one night, he was driving a taxi cab, and we got to talk about Jolly Roll, he picked us up over there near where the jungle in was. Oh, yeah. And he said, you know, do you know about Jolly Roll? And I said, well, sure. I said, well, I used to play with him. Is that right? And he played with him apparently a lot. Was it clarinet? He played the reeds, he said.

Well, maybe he was a man, but whoever it was disappointed him. He wrote a tune, and, uh, one night, one night or one afternoon, I tried to get around there when the place wasn't busy, so I wouldn't be interfering with anything. I got around there one afternoon, and he played this thing through, what it was, and I said, well, what's that? He said, a little piece I composed. Composed for a clarinet player, and he was going to meet me down at the United Recording Company down there, and he says he never showed up.…
I think it's often just about the business that he did at Tony Jackson's that he heard Tony do in New Orleans, and then Tony did again in Chicago when he saw him there.
